input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed on the whole package. I read input/brief.md (formalities only: no priority claim, no federally sponsored R&D — matching "Not applicable." in draft/02 and draft/03), input/conversation.md (a single USER passage that is a truncated copy of the disclosure, ending mid-sentence at "retained by", adding nothing beyond it), and input/disclosure.md, which I treated as the sole authority for technical matter. I then built a complete ledger and traced: (a) every limitation of all seventeen claims — apparatus claims 1–11 and method claims 12–17, including the closed-on-itself circulation path, the lid-gasket ordering of claim 2/13, the resilient-feet/ledge retention of claim 3/14, the opposed-cassette geometry of claim 4, the one-piece module removal of claims 5/15, the condensate channel and discharge openings of claim 6/16, the wick and pull tab of claims 7–8, and the indicator chain of claims 9–11/17 — each to an affirmative disclosure sentence; (b) all thirty reference numerals in draft/numerals.md, confirming each is defined once, used consistently with one meaning, appears in at least one figure brief, and that no numeral appears in the description or a brief without a table entry; (c) all seven figure briefs and the Brief Description in draft/07, confirming the FIG. 2 five-broken-circle scheme matches the FIG. 3–FIG. 7 region designations one-for-one, that the section designation "2-2" is repeated identically in the FIG. 1 brief (line with the designation at each end and arrows toward the rear), the FIG. 2 source-view brief, and the drawing description, and that each brief's "Numerals shown" list matches the numerals actually verbalized in that brief; (d) the description, summary, and abstract for term-for-term agreement with the claims (registered position, peripheral outlet openings overlapping side supply passages, depending indexing rib, mating channel, resilient feet, ledges, condensate discharge openings, latched exposed position). No drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains in the application text, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language was used to justify a renderer's shape choice. Materials, counts, proportions, operating conditions, and results were checked: no dimensions, temperatures, or materials beyond the disclosed "rigid" frame, "compressible" gasket, "resilient" feet, and "absorbent" wick appear, and the two optional features (wick, mechanical exposure indicator) match the disclosure's own statement that they are optional. Background prior-art characterizations were not required to trace to the inventor. Two defects remain. First, the figure briefs verbalize an undisclosed position for the rib-and-channel registration joint: FIG. 2 places the tongue "at the centre of the width" and FIG. 3 places the mating channel "in the upper web of the frame 42", i.e. directly over the plenum between the opposed cassettes into which the central inlet opens, whereas the disclosure says only that "the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame". That is a relative location for a functional joint and a boundary of the air-dividing space, and is substantive even though the brief calls the geometry schematic. Second, the detailed description asserts that "no electrical power, battery, or logging device is required for the indication", a comparative attribute no inventor passage states. Everything else in the ledger — including the bore through the shell wall in FIG. 7, the ledge/foot contact in FIG. 4, the outlet-and-condensate openings at the duct lower end in FIG. 5, and the condensate trough placement in FIG. 6 — traces to an affirmative disclosure sentence or is a minimally specific depiction of an affirmatively disclosed functional part.

findings.title: Figure briefs verbalize an undisclosed position for the indexing rib and mating channel
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (Insulated lid 60 bullet); figures/FIG-3.md (Mating channel 52 bullet and the closing statement)
findings.detail: The registration joint is given a specific location across the frame and a specific relationship to the air-dividing space between the cassettes. FIG. 2 states the tongue depends "at the centre of the width" into the recess in the module's upper surface, and FIG. 3 states that the mating channel 52 is a recess "in the upper web of the frame 42" — the web that closes the plenum which FIG. 3 itself describes as "continuous upward with the blank open space between the two cassettes 44" — and that "the lid 60 lies above the upper web of the frame 42". The disclosure discloses the rib and the channel as parts, and discloses that the rib shifts the module, but never states where the channel lies on the frame or that it is formed in the roof of the space into which the central inlet air divides. Placing a registration joint on the centreline, over the flow-dividing plenum, is a relative location for a functional joint and a flow boundary, and is substantive notwithstanding the "shown schematically" label. No affirmative USER passage exists for it; the disclosure's only sentences on the joint are silent on position.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-3.md): "Mating channel 52: an upwardly open recess in the upper web of the frame 42, shown schematically and bounded on both sides by hatched frame material." and "The rib 62 is engaged in the channel 52 while the lid 60 lies above the upper web of the frame 42." Candidate (figures/FIG-2.md): "an unnumbered short tongue depending from its underside at the centre of the width into an unnumbered recess in the upper surface of the module 40". Nearest source passage, which shows the gap (input/disclosure.md): "The lid carries a depending indexing rib. As the lid closes, the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame and shifts the thermal module into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages." — no position on the frame, no relationship to the space between the cassettes, is given.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, replace "an unnumbered short tongue depending from its underside at the centre of the width into an unnumbered recess in the upper surface of the module 40" with "an unnumbered short tongue depending from its underside into an unnumbered recess in the upper surface of the module 40". In figures/FIG-3.md, replace "Mating channel 52: an upwardly open recess in the upper web of the frame 42, shown schematically and bounded on both sides by hatched frame material." with "Mating channel 52: an upwardly open recess in an upper surface of the frame 42, shown schematically and bounded on both sides by hatched frame material." and replace "The rib 62 is engaged in the channel 52 while the lid 60 lies above the upper web of the frame 42." with "The rib 62 is engaged in the channel 52 while the lid 60 lies above the frame 42." No change is needed in draft/07-drawings.md, whose "central upper region" designates the enlarged region by reference to the disclosed central inlet opening rather than to the channel.

findings.title: Untraced statement that no electrical power, battery, or logging device is required
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Mechanical exposure indicator" section, final paragraph
findings.detail: The description asserts a negative attribute of the indicator that no inventor passage states. The disclosure calls the indicator "mechanical" and describes a stem, a temperature-responsive latch, and a spring, but says nothing about electrical power, batteries, or logging devices. The comparison to a logging device in particular imports a prior-art contrast into the invention description; it appears nowhere in the disclosure or in the single USER passage of the conversation.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The thermal condition being reported is taken directly from a phase-change cassette 44, that is, from the reserve that actually conditions the payload, and no electrical power, battery, or logging device is required for the indication." Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md): "The shell includes a mechanical exposure indicator visible from outside. An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch. ... The indicator does not control airflow." — no statement about power, batteries, or logging devices.
findings.fix: Delete the trailing clause so the sentence reads: "The thermal condition being reported is taken directly from a phase-change cassette 44, that is, from the reserve that actually conditions the payload."
